investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-16T07:07–07:15Z because every pod submitted to create a remote agent was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes, and the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector requirements. Because no pod could be scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never progressed to VM provisioning, and the eval timed out after ~147–153 seconds without writing any required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — the scheduler explicitly reports resource exhaustion on the 2 kata-capable nodes and affinity mismatch on the other 4.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message with 142s stuck duration, confirming the condition persisted across sequential probe runs.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message with 144s stuck duration, confirming the condition persisted into a third sequential probe run ending at 07:15:06Z.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=153925, status=fail — the probe ran for ~154 seconds before failing, consistent with a scheduling timeout rather than an immediate API error.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming the agent pod never reached a state where the runner could collect VM or agent identity data.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after resolving orgId; if the resulting pod is never scheduled, no downstream evidence can be written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: the contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'], neither of which can be satisfied when the pod never starts.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing running remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero allocatable units for new probe pods.

[Likely] The 4 non-kata nodes have a node affinity or node selector requirement (e.g., a label such as kata-capable=true or peerpods=enabled) that they do not carry, permanently excluding them from scheduling remote-agent pods regardless of available CPU/memory.

[Possible] A recent scale-down, node failure, or maintenance event reduced the number of kata-capable nodes from a higher count to 2, shrinking total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity below the level needed to absorb both production workloads and eval probes simultaneously.

[Possible] The eval probe pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm is set to a value that cannot be satisfied even when nodes have partial remaining capacity (e.g., requesting more than 1 unit per pod).

[Lower likelihood] A misconfiguration in node affinity/selector on the pod template used by createAgent causes pods to target only the 2 kata nodes while simultaneously over-requesting their vm resource, making scheduling structurally impossible until capacity is freed or nodes are added.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed that kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is not exhausted (i.e., allocatable > used on at least one eligible node), the capacity-exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a pod spec misconfiguration or API-level failure.
If the eval passed on an immediate re-run without any infrastructure change, it would suggest a transient scheduling contention rather than sustained capacity exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed, a shared infrastructure capacity problem would be less likely and a check-specific configuration issue would be more likely.

If the 4 non-kata nodes were found to carry the required node labels, the affinity/selector mismatch hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would be limited to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes.

If no existing pods are consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a node-level resource reporting error or a misconfigured resource limit on the nodes themselves.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on each cluster node and alerts when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), providing early warning before scheduling failures occur.

Add a cluster-node-affinity eval that verifies the expected number of nodes carry the required remote-agent scheduling labels, catching node label drift or unexpected node removals before they cause pod scheduling failures.

Add a pending-pod-age eval that detects remote-agent pods stuck in Pending state for more than a configurable threshold (e.g., 60 seconds) and surfaces the scheduler rejection reason as structured evidence, enabling faster diagnosis without waiting for the full probe timeout.

Consider adding a pre-flight capacity check within the remote-agent-create probe itself that queries node allocatable resources before attempting agent creation, allowing the eval to report a more specific failure mode (capacity exhaustion vs. API error vs. timeout) rather than a generic pod-stuck message.

investigation.title: Remote Agents eval failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity exhausted — all three remote-agent checks unschedulable
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 07:10 and 07:15 UTC on 2026-07-16 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~142–147 s), preventing the eval runner from reaching the state-polling phase and producing any required evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266 (line 264): contract requires [orgId, agentId, readyState, state] — none present because agent pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: both nodes that carry the kata peer-pods VM resource class are at capacity, and no preemption victims exist to free slots. All three eval checks hit this simultaneously, indicating a cluster-wide shortage rather than a transient single-node issue.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the four remaining nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. If the selector was recently tightened or node labels were changed, the effective schedulable node count may have dropped from a larger pool to just the two kata-capable nodes, making exhaustion more likely.

Tertiary — eval concurrency: all three remote-agent checks ran within the same ~5-minute window (07:10–07:15 UTC) and each attempted to create a remote agent pod. If the cluster had only 2 available VM slots and all three probes competed for them simultaneously, contention alone could exhaust capacity even if baseline availability was marginal.

Lower confidence — transient cluster event (node drain, maintenance, or scale-down): a node could have been cordoned or removed just before the eval window, reducing the kata-capable node count and triggering exhaustion. No node-event evidence is present in the packet to confirm this.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-16T07:07–07:15Z because every pod submitted to create a remote agent was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes, and the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector requirements. Because no pod could be scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never progressed to VM provisioning, and the eval timed out after ~147–153 seconds without writing any required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — the scheduler explicitly reports resource exhaustion on the 2 kata-capable nodes and affinity mismatch on the other 4.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message with 142s stuck duration, confirming the condition persisted across sequential probe runs.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message with 144s stuck duration, confirming the condition persisted into a third sequential probe run ending at 07:15:06Z.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=153925, status=fail — the probe ran for ~154 seconds before failing, consistent with a scheduling timeout rather than an immediate API error.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming the agent pod never reached a state where the runner could collect VM or agent identity data.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after resolving orgId; if the resulting pod is never scheduled, no downstream evidence can be written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: the contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'], neither of which can be satisfied when the pod never starts.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing running remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero allocatable units for new probe pods.

[Likely] The 4 non-kata nodes have a node affinity or node selector requirement (e.g., a label such as kata-capable=true or peerpods=enabled) that they do not carry, permanently excluding them from scheduling remote-agent pods regardless of available CPU/memory.

[Possible] A recent scale-down, node failure, or maintenance event reduced the number of kata-capable nodes from a higher count to 2, shrinking total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity below the level needed to absorb both production workloads and eval probes simultaneously.

[Possible] The eval probe pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm is set to a value that cannot be satisfied even when nodes have partial remaining capacity (e.g., requesting more than 1 unit per pod).

[Lower likelihood] A misconfiguration in node affinity/selector on the pod template used by createAgent causes pods to target only the 2 kata nodes while simultaneously over-requesting their vm resource, making scheduling structurally impossible until capacity is freed or nodes are added.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed that kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is not exhausted (i.e., allocatable > used on at least one eligible node), the capacity-exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a pod spec misconfiguration or API-level failure.
If the eval passed on an immediate re-run without any infrastructure change, it would suggest a transient scheduling contention rather than sustained capacity exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed, a shared infrastructure capacity problem would be less likely and a check-specific configuration issue would be more likely.

If the 4 non-kata nodes were found to carry the required node labels, the affinity/selector mismatch hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would be limited to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes.

If no existing pods are consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a node-level resource reporting error or a misconfigured resource limit on the nodes themselves.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on each cluster node and alerts when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), providing early warning before scheduling failures occur.

Add a cluster-node-affinity eval that verifies the expected number of nodes carry the required remote-agent scheduling labels, catching node label drift or unexpected node removals before they cause pod scheduling failures.

Add a pending-pod-age eval that detects remote-agent pods stuck in Pending state for more than a configurable threshold (e.g., 60 seconds) and surfaces the scheduler rejection reason as structured evidence, enabling faster diagnosis without waiting for the full probe timeout.

Consider adding a pre-flight capacity check within the remote-agent-create probe itself that queries node allocatable resources before attempting agent creation, allowing the eval to report a more specific failure mode (capacity exhaustion vs. API error vs. timeout) rather than a generic pod-stuck message.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 07:10 and 07:15 UTC on 2026-07-16 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state was fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~142–147 s), preventing the eval runner from reaching the state-polling phase and producing any required evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: both nodes that carry the kata peer-pods VM resource class are at capacity, and no preemption victims exist to free slots. All three eval checks hit this simultaneously, indicating a cluster-wide shortage rather than a transient single-node issue.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the four remaining nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. If the selector was recently tightened or node labels were changed, the effective schedulable node count may have dropped from a larger pool to just the two kata-capable nodes, making exhaustion more likely.

Tertiary — eval concurrency: all three remote-agent checks ran within the same ~5-minute window (07:10–07:15 UTC) and each attempted to create a remote agent pod. If the cluster had only 2 available VM slots and all three probes competed for them simultaneously, contention alone could exhaust capacity even if baseline availability was marginal.

Lower confidence — transient cluster event (node drain, maintenance, or scale-down): a node could have been cordoned or removed just before the eval window, reducing the kata-capable node count and triggering exhaustion. No node-event evidence is present in the packet to confirm this.

If the remote-agent pod spec's nodeSelector or affinity rules were recently changed to exclude the two kata-capable nodes, the root cause would be a configuration change rather than capacity exhaustion.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed between 07:10 and 07:15 UTC on 2026-07-16 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler error: the 6-node production cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, both of which reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No pod was ever scheduled, so the eval runner never reached the agent creation step and produced zero evidence output against the expected contract (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message).
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was exhausted on the only 2 eligible nodes in the 6-node cluster, and preemption was not possible (no lower-priority victims found). This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents swarm VM pool in the production-api environment. The eval never progressed past pod scheduling, so all five required evidence fields are absent and the expected-output contract assertion ("hello from aura" in message) could not be evaluated. This is an eval-layer signal of an infrastructure capacity problem; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run the remote-agent-runtime eval probe in isolation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the scheduling failure is persistent or has self-resolved. A continued Unschedulable error confirms ongoing resource exhaustion; a pass confirms transient capacity contention.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run all three remote-agents sibling checks together
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the scheduling failure is shared across all remote-agent pod types or isolated to a specific check, helping localize whether the issue is the VM pool, node affinity, or a specific pod spec.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Query kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on all cluster nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly proves or disproves the resource-exhaustion hypothesis. If both kata-capable nodes show 0 allocatable or 100% allocated, exhaustion is confirmed. Node names and current pod consumers should be captured.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List all pods currently holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations in the production cluster
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether a stuck or leaked pod from a prior eval run is holding the resource allocation, which would explain why preemption found no victims (no lower-priority pods to evict).

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Rules out node degradation (NotReady, MemoryPressure, DiskPressure) as a secondary cause that would prevent scheduling even if the resource counter shows available capacity.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 kata-capable nodes shows non-zero allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm with no current consumers, the resource-exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a node condition or scheduler plugin bug.

If the remote-agent pod spec requests more kata.peerpods.io/vm units than the per-node maximum, the failure would be structural (spec misconfiguration) rather than transient capacity exhaustion — confirmed by comparing pod resource requests against node capacity.

If a subsequent eval run immediately succeeds without any cluster changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a prior eval's pod released its allocation just after this run started), weakening the exhaustion hypothesis.
If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass in a follow-up run, the failure is isolated to the runtime check rather than a shared scheduling constraint.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are reconfigured to accept remote-agent pods and scheduling succeeds, the root cause was node affinity misconfiguration rather than resource exhaustion on the 2 kata nodes.
